chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman with a temporary marriage, would it be Permissible for him that he marries her daughter? He (peace be upon him) said: No.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry the daughter of a woman with whom one has had a temporary marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific prohibition of marrying the daughter of a woman with whom one has contracted a temporary marriage (mut'ah), establishing a clear legal parallel to permanent marriage. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the kinship ties formed through mut'ah are sufficient to render the daughter prohibited, ensuring consistency in marital laws. This ruling underscores the structural integrity of family relations in Shia jurisprudence, where the union itself creates the barrier regardless of consummation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the man who marries the woman with a temporary marriage, would it be Permissible for him that he marries her daughter?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who married a woman in manner of al-Mut‘ah; if it is permissible for him to marry her daughter. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it is not permissible.’”
